D006-D010_h001.question:
For about ten months now, my wife keeps saying I’m “not myself.” I feel constantly on edge, like everyone is irritating me—students, colleagues, even my kids. Tiny things set me off; an email with a minor criticism can make me snap. At the same time, I’m strangely driven. I’ll stay up half the night planning three new courses, starting a book proposal, redesigning my whole syllabus, then abandoning each halfway through because a “better” idea pops up. My office is full of half-finished projects and notes everywhere. It’s gotten to the point where I’ve missed deadlines and committee work, and my chair has commented on my “erratic follow-through.”

For the last eight months, I’ve also had these odd sensations, like something is crawling on my arms or tapping my shoulder when no one is there. I’ve started to worry that someone in the department—or higher up—is monitoring me, maybe tracking my computer or bugging my office. Sometimes I catch myself using words that I know aren’t real, like “textual shimmerlines” or “mind-static,” but they make perfect sense to me at the time.

More recently, maybe three months, I’ve pulled back from friends and colleagues. I avoid faculty gatherings and barely return calls. I lie in bed thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up, not that I’d do anything, but there’s this recurring wish to just stop existing. It’s making it harder to teach and to be present with my family.
D006-D010_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder
D006-D010_h001.answer: C & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) & Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006-D010_h002.question:
It’s been almost a year now that I’ve been “off.” Around ten months ago I started feeling like I was on top of the world all the time. I’d wake up buzzing with energy, like I’d had ten cups of coffee, even on days off. I couldn’t sit still, I’d start cleaning the garage at 3 a.m. or planning new drills for the crew. Little things would grab my attention—someone tapping a pen, a flicker of light, a radio clicking on in another room—and I’d lose my train of thought.

About eight months ago, I started seeing people who weren’t there. Sometimes it’s figures in the bay at the station, or in the corner of our bedroom. I’ll be talking and my words just fall apart; my wife says I start stringing sounds together and she can’t follow what I’m saying at all.

Lately—maybe the last three months—it flipped. I stopped caring about the gym, about shifts, even about calls. I just felt empty and useless. A few weeks back I put all my pain meds aside and wrote a note; my wife found them before I could do anything. I’m still working, but barely holding it together.
D006-D010_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder
D006-D010_h002.answer: C & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) & Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006-D010_h003.question:
It’s hard to explain this clearly… my thoughts jump around a lot, so I might go off track. For about ten months now I’ve been bouncing between feeling on top of the world and then snapping at people over nothing. One hour I’m sketching five versions of a façade, pacing around the office, full of ideas, talking too fast; the next I’m furious because someone moved a sample board. I can’t sit still in meetings, my mind keeps hopping to the next project, then some random detail, and I lose the thread of the conversation.

Around eight months ago I started hearing this… commentary. Sometimes it’s like a couple of voices just behind me, talking about what I’m doing or telling me I’m “wasting time,” even when the room is quiet. There’s also this woman I know professionally—an engineer on a project—I’ve become convinced she has feelings for me. Little things she says or emails feel like secret messages. My wife keeps telling me I’m imagining it.

Lately, for about three months, the drive I used to have for my work is gone. Even finishing a big competition entry felt meaningless. On bad days, when I’m up on a scaffold or near traffic, I get this sudden pull to just step off or walk into the street. It’s not exactly planned, more like an urge that scares me, but it passes. I’m still coming into the office, but my team has started quietly taking things off my plate because I’m either too wired or too checked out to really handle them.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder
D006-D010_h003.answer: C & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) & Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006-D010_h004.question:
It’s hard to explain because it all kind of overlaps. For about the past year I’ve felt like I’m on this strange rollercoaster. A lot of the time I’m way up — almost too up. I’ll wake up buzzing, like I’ve had six cups of coffee, even when I haven’t slept much. At school I can’t sit still; I’m pacing around the classroom, starting a bulletin board, then jumping to new lesson plans, then reorganizing cubbies, but nothing actually gets finished. I feel almost giddy for no reason, talking a mile a minute, and my husband says I jump from topic to topic and never really answer what he’s asking.

Around the same time, I started smelling things that no one else can smell — like smoke or this sickly sweet perfume — at home, in the classroom, even in the car. It makes me wonder if it’s some kind of sign. Sometimes I’ll hear kids whispering or see a comment online and feel like it’s secretly about me, like they’re hinting at something I’m supposed to pick up on.

Then, for the last few months, I’ve also been dropping into these really dark periods. I stop texting friends back, let my family’s calls go to voicemail, and just stay in the bedroom after work. I’ve felt so hopeless that I’ve thought through exactly how and where I might kill myself, down to when my husband would be out so he wouldn’t be the one to find me. On those days I can barely manage the class, and my lesson plans fall apart. It’s confusing because the high-energy, almost “too good” days and the really low ones seem to mix together over time, and I can’t tell where one ends and the other starts.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder

D006-D010_h005.question:
I’ve been out here on my own for a few years, but things really started getting strange about ten months ago. At first I just felt keyed up all the time, like I was plugged into a generator. I’d pace the stairs up and down the tower for hours, barely sleep, jumping from checking the light, to cleaning, to writing notes I never finish. I can’t stick with one task; my mind keeps skittering off. Little things set me off too—if the radio crackles or a bulb blows, I snap and start swearing, sometimes throw tools. It’s not like me.

Around eight months back, the “voices” started. It’s mostly at night, when the fog horn is quiet—I hear someone calling my name or talking just behind me, but when I check, there’s no one. Sometimes they sound like they’re commenting on what I’m doing. There’s also this woman from the supply boat—I’m convinced she’s been sending me signals, like extra-long horn blasts, that mean she’s thinking about me. I know everyone would say that’s crazy, but it feels…certain.

The past three months, when the wind dies and everything goes still, it’s like the energy collapses. I just stay in my bunk between rounds, don’t answer the radio unless I have to. I’ve stopped calling my brother; it feels pointless. I keep thinking it’d be easier if a storm just took the tower and I didn’t have to wake up for the next shift. I’m still doing the basic checks so nothing catastrophic happens, but it takes everything I’ve got.
D006-D010_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder
D006-D010_h005.answer: C & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) & Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006-D010_h006.question:
I’d say this all really started about a year and a half, maybe closer to two years ago. I run a used car lot, and back then business was already stressful, but I started getting this feeling like it didn’t matter anyway, like everything’s heading for some giant disaster. It’s not just “things are bad” — it feels like the world is sort of winding down, like there’s no real future. I catch myself thinking, “What’s the point of selling cars if none of this is going to be here?”

Around the same time I began smelling things that no one else seems to notice — like burning rubber, gasoline leaks, or this rotten, chemical kind of smell in my office or even at home. I’ll go around checking the lot, the wiring, the garage, asking my guys if they smell it, and they look at me like I’m overreacting.

I’m on edge all the time now. The smallest thing — a customer haggling too much, my ex texting about the kids — sets me off. I pace a lot, can’t sit in my office chair for more than a few minutes. I’ll start repainting a car, then jump to reorganizing the keys, then start drafting ads online, all at once, leaving everything half-done. There are stretches where I barely sleep for several nights, but it doesn’t even bother me in the moment — I just keep working, cleaning, making plans. It’s only later, when deals fall through and the lot’s a mess, that I realize how much it’s messing up my work and my life.

A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D006-D010_h006.answer: D & C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) & Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006-D010_h007.question:

I keep catching myself thinking I’m meant for bigger things, like I’ve got some special gift for building stuff, like other people just can’t see it yet. It sounds cocky, I know, but it feels… true in my gut.

Around the same time I stopped really sleeping. I can go most of the night with maybe an hour or two of rest and still feel wired, like I’ve had ten coffees. I’ll start three or four projects at once—reorganizing the crew schedule, drawing up plans for a new business, fixing things around the house at 2 a.m.—but I bounce around and don’t actually finish much. My mind jumps so fast I can’t stay on one thing, even in safety meetings; my guys have had to repeat stuff to me.

What really freaks me out is the feeling on my skin—like bugs crawling or someone brushing past me when no one’s there. It’s been coming and going the whole time, same as the “I’m special” feeling. My wife says I’m not myself and that I’m working myself into the ground, but I don’t feel tired—even when I probably should.

D006-D010_h008.question:
